'''Alton Ford Jr.''' (May 29, 1981 – April 2, 2018) was an American professional [[basketball]] player who played in the [[National Basketball Association]] and other leagues. He last played for the [[NBA D-League]] team the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]].

Ford was born in [[Houston, Texas]] and attended Houston ISD [[Milby High School]].

He was selected 51st overall in the [[2001 NBA draft]] by the [[Phoenix Suns]]. He played with the Phoenix Suns from [[2001-02 NBA season|2001]] to [[2002-03 NBA season|2003]], and then with the [[Houston Rockets]] in the [[2003-04 NBA season]]. Ford played a total of 73 NBA games (64 for Phoenix and 9 for Houston) with career averages of 2.5 points and 1.7 rebounds. His final NBA game was on January 3, 2004, in an 84–63 win over the Utah Jazz where he played for a little under 2 minutes and recorded no stats.

He played overseas from 2004 to 2008.

==Personal life and death==
Ford and his wife, Victoria had four children.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/cougars/article/Milby-star-Alton-Ford-dies-at-36-12803554.php|title = Milby star Alton Ford dies at 36|date = April 3, 2018}}</ref>

Ford died of [[lymphoma]], a form of blood cancer, on April 2, 2018. He was 36.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/cougars/article/Alton-Ford-Milby-UH-Rockets-dies-at-36-12801823.php?ipid=happening |title=Alton Ford, former player for Milby, UH, Rockets, dies at 36 |work=Houston Chronicle |first=Joseph |last=Duarte |date=April 3, 2018}}</ref> His funeral was held on April 5, 2018.<ref>[http://claytonfuneralhomes.com/tribute/details/1667/Alton-Ford/obituary.html Alton Ford, Jr.]</ref>
